Name: BashBench (BashCoder-R1 2026)
Includes Eval?: No. It ships tests, but they do not work.
Notes: Do not use this as an evaluation. The harness saves the model's script to solution.sh and then runs the task's test.sh. None of the 1081 released test scripts ever read solution.sh, so the score does not depend on the generated code at all. Each test just re-runs the reference commands itself. Three checks on the authors' own published results confirm it. 178 of 179 tasks get an identical verdict from 7 different models ranging from 3B to 32B. Every model scores 93 to 94 percent once its code is extractable. Where a model wrote different code for the same prompt, 67 of 68 got the same verdict anyway. The published spread from 6.7 to 93.9 percent only reflects whether a model emitted a parseable code block. Separately, 709 of the 773 single-line tasks (91.7 percent) appear word for word in the training data shipped in the same release, though the paper claims the tasks are completely isolated from training data. The 179 multi-line tasks are genuinely clean. Still useful as data: 952 English prompts and reference solutions with a real single and multi-line split. The reference solutions are themselves LLM-generated. arXiv 2606.27733 (ISSTA 2026). zenodo.org/records/18408692. CC-BY-4.0.

Name: BashBench (Redwood / Ctrl-Z 2025)
Notes: A different project that shares the name with the 2026 BashBench above. 257 sysadmin tasks from Unix StackExchange, each solvable in up to 15 commands run in sequence, graded by public and private Python tests. Built for AI-control research. arXiv 2504.10374. bashcontrol.com

Name: Terminal-Bench 2.0
Notes: Every task is an English instruction plus a Docker environment, a test suite, and an oracle solution. 16 categories. Runs on the Harbor harness. ICLR 2026. arXiv 2601.11868. github.com/harbor-framework/terminal-bench

Name: Terminal-Bench Pro (Alibaba)
Notes: A harder variant of Terminal-Bench. Needs a cloud execution backend such as Modal. huggingface.co/datasets/alibabagroup/terminal-bench-pro

Name: Long-Horizon Terminal-Bench (LHTB)
Notes: 46 long-horizon tasks. The verifiers are hidden by design. The harness keeps resuming the session with verifier feedback until the task passes or times out. huggingface.co/datasets/IntelligenceLab/Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench

Name: TerminalWorld
Notes: 1530 tasks reverse-engineered from public repos. Each one has an English instruction, an oracle solution, state-based tests, and a reproducible Docker environment. Also ships a 200-task human-verified subset. huggingface.co/datasets/EuniAI/TerminalWorld

Name: InterCode-Bash (IC-Bash)
Notes: 200 tasks run against 4 Docker filesystems. Scored by execution: a git diff of the container state, an MD5 of file contents, and TF-IDF on stdout. Do not use it as held-out data. The tasks were drawn from NL2Bash, so the whole InterCode line already sits inside the corpora Bash models are trained on. Measured against a 78000-command union of the seven main public corpora, westenfelder/InterCode-Corrections is 100 percent contained and epinnock/intercode-nl2bash-curated is 63.8 percent, against 0.1 to 0.2 percent for benchmarks written against a real environment. Filtering cannot repair this, and a score here measures memorisation as much as capability. NeurIPS 2023. arXiv 2306.14898. github.com/princeton-nlp/intercode

Name: laion/stackexchange-unix-sandboxes-verified
Notes: 10000 computer-use tasks from Unix and Linux StackExchange. Each sandbox ships an LLM judge rather than deterministic tests, so the verdicts are softer than a real pass or fail suite. Repackaged from DCAgent/stackexchange-unix-sandboxes-skywork-response.

Name: nvidia/Nemotron-Terminal-Synthetic-Tasks
Notes: Synthetic terminal tasks. Each has a verification suite at tests/test.sh. Ships 9 standard Docker images and a sandboxed tmux. Companion to Nemotron-Terminal-Corpus. arXiv 2602.21193

Name: nvidia/Nemotron-Terminal-Corpus
Notes: 366154 execution traces across 4 configs: dataset_adapters 226313, skill_based_easy 44809, skill_based_medium 89343, and skill_based_mixed 5689. This is a trace corpus for fine-tuning, not a set of English and command pairs. Re-uploaded word for word by CathleenTico, txchmechanicus, and nick007x. arXiv 2602.21193

Name: Eccentricity/bashbench2
Notes: 637 tasks. Each one ships a dockerfile, tests, and a setup script. Successor in spirit to the Redwood BashBench.

Name: Eccentricity/basharena2 (BashArena)
Notes: 4684 task descriptions. A control setting for highly privileged AI agents. arXiv 2512.15688

Name: tiararodney/posix-sdc
Notes: 4765 synthetic POSIX shell trajectories. 65 percent of the reference solutions use more than one command. Has checker, fixtures, verified, and outcome fields, and every trajectory's outcome was checked against real filesystem state. The single and multi-line split is estimated from a 2975-row sample.

Name: saurabh5/rlvr-code-data-bash
Notes: The best find in the survey. 133247 rows, of which 66624 have a bash solution, and all of those are multi-line function definitions rather than one-liners. 66004 of them are unique. The columns are translated_problem for the English, translated_solution for the bash, and translated_test_cases for the tests. Measured 0 percent overlap with NL2Bash, NL2CMD, NL2SH-ALFA, and tldr, so its lineage is independent. This is the largest multi-line bash source with test cases found anywhere in the survey.

Name: AgentBench OS
Notes: Agents act in a real Ubuntu Docker shell. About 1200 documented tasks with setup scripts and checking utilities, though the released eval subset is much smaller. ICLR 2024. arXiv 2308.03688. github.com/THUDM/AgentBench

Name: Local-LLMs-4-Bash (NDSS LASTX 2026)
Notes: KU Leuven. A corrected and extended version of the InterCode-ALFA 300-task test set. They fixed 18 tasks that were scored wrongly and flagged 12 more that cannot be verified at all. Adds realistic incorrect samples and a better scoring scheme. Also releases two RAG corpora: 981 environment man pages and 9812 reasoning examples. github.com/JefJacobs00/Local-LLMs-4-Bash

Name: b-mc2/cli-commands-explained
Notes: 16098 rows scraped from commandlinefu.com. Each row is a real command with a human-written title, a human-written description, and votes. 15679 unique commands. Only 1 to 2 percent of its commands overlap with NL2Bash, NL2SH-ALFA, NL2CMD, or tldr, which makes it one of the few large sets that is genuinely independent rather than a remix of the others.

Name: ajibawa-2023/Shell-Code-Large
Notes: 639183 rows of real shell scripts from GitHub. 98.4 percent are multi-line, measured on a 103042-row sample containing 27824 unique scripts. 0 percent overlap with every English to bash corpus. This is by far the largest multi-line bash source found, but it is code only. There is a language column and no English instruction, so it needs pairing before it can be used.

Name: jragsdale1/ShIO-bash-26.1
Notes: Not an English to bash set. 4803184 rows pairing a command with its stdout, exit code, and environment state change, recorded from ShIOEnv, a Gymnasium bash environment. Covers 86 Linux utilities on Ubuntu 24.04. 0.1 percent multi-line, measured on a 316245-row sample with 312736 unique commands. 0 percent overlap with every English corpus. Relevant to our own pipeline because it is ready-made execution ground truth for real coreutils.

Name: Mitchins/NL-SHELL-MULTI
Notes: Not a new corpus. A documented merge of NL2Bash, tldr-pages, and the NL2SH-ALFA train split. Hashing confirms it fully contains jiacheng-ye/nl2bash (7559 commands) and TRamesh2/NL2CMD (8513). 63862 unique commands.

Name: AryaYT/nl2shell-training-v3
Notes: 12834 pairs, 12799 of them unique. 8 percent multi-line. Heavily derived: 59 percent of its commands are in NL2Bash and 65 percent are in TRamesh2/NL2CMD, leaving roughly 35 percent that looks new. 961 rows are flagged as expert-curated.

Name: AryaYT/nl2shell-terminal-bench
Notes: 7509 synthetic trajectories, each a think step, a command, and a verify step. Every one carries a verification command that checks whether the step worked. Synthetic and not human-validated.

Name: Frost2o24/bash-instruct-55k
Notes: 55000 synthetic instruction-tuning rows. A companion set, bash-instruct-II-55k, adds 54803 more. The provenance is not documented, so treat it with caution.

Name: NickIBrody/linux-shell-corpus-ru-en
Notes: A bilingual Russian and English Linux shell assistant dataset. 25000 rows.

Name: mecha-org/linux-command-dataset
Notes: 8669 rows with 7500 unique commands and almost nothing multi-line. Only 1 to 2 percent overlap with the canonical corpora.

Name: emirkaanozdemr/bash_command_data_6K
Notes: 6153 rows, 4451 of them unique, 11.1 percent multi-line. Roughly 1 to 3 percent overlap with the canonical corpora.

Name: AnishJoshi/nl2bash-custom
Notes: 24569 non-empty rows with 12659 unique commands, 6.6 percent multi-line. This is a merge, and it is the bigger set: it contains all 8513 commands of TRamesh2/NL2CMD, 7558 of the 7559 in NL2Bash, and all 6381 of rlawltjd/korean-nl2bash. About 4100 of its commands appear in none of the seven root corpora. If you take this one you already have those three in full.

Name: Edoigtrd/tldr-pages
Notes: 5274 rows taken from the tldr-pages project, which is community-simplified man pages. 5012 unique commands. This is the raw tldr source that both NL2SH-ALFA and NL-SHELL-MULTI draw on, and 30 percent of it is already inside NL2SH-ALFA.

Name: datasetter458/diverse-bash-dataset-extended
Notes: 9351 rows, 8340 of them unique. The same author also published diverse-bash-dataset (4912 rows), w3schools-bash-tutorial-QAs (417), and bash-reference-manual-general-QAs (1276).

Name: huytd189/command-line-suggestions
Notes: 3334 rows with 2855 unique commands. About 1 percent overlap with the canonical corpora.

Name: Euroswarms/bash
Notes: Low quality, and do not count the headline number. It advertises 1000000 rows, but a 483553-row sample contains only 4618 unique responses, and those responses are fragments of the Bash reference manual rather than actual commands.

Name: missvector/linux-commands (LinLM)
Notes: 71775 rows but only 5451 unique commands, so the file is roughly 13 times duplicated internally. The same file has been re-uploaded word for word 5 more times under other accounts.

Name: AuricErgeson/text-to-shell-dataset
Notes: 697 rows, 492 of them unique.

Name: aelhalili/bash-commands-dataset
Notes: 840 rows, 472 of them unique. Roughly 5 to 12 percent overlap with the canonical corpora.

Name: byroneverson/shell-cmd-instruct
Notes: 500 rows, 377 of them unique.

Name: kth8/bash-toolcalls
Notes: 862 rows. Bash commands framed as tool calls.

Name: epinnock/intercode-nl2bash-curated
Notes: 200 hand-curated pairs of a query and a gold command, reproducing the InterCode NL2Bash set. 60 percent of its commands are inside NL2SH-ALFA. Contaminated by construction, so do not use it as held-out data.

Name: ZygAI/zygai_linux_commands
Notes: 254 rows. Bilingual Lithuanian and English.

Name: tmskss/linux-man-pages-tldr-summarized
Notes: 481 man pages summarised in tldr style.

Name: iselabvn/Linux-terminal-tool-calling
Notes: 600 rows. A Linux terminal framed as tool calling.

Name: adeelahmad/bash-agent-grpo-pairs
Notes: 11745 rows, all of them unique, and 46.2 percent multi-line, which is unusually high for a set of this kind. Read the ground_truth column rather than answer, because answer is wrapped in reasoning tags. Measured 0 percent overlap with all canonical corpora. It is synthetic, so the quality is unvetted, but it is one of the few large sets with a real multi-line share.

Name: lisayan/rlvr-bash-terminal-bench
Notes: Not a task set. 1120 model rollouts on Terminal-Bench tasks, each recording reward, test_passed, test_failed, and pass_rate. Useful as difficulty labels rather than as source data. Only 10.4 percent scored a full reward.

Name: CmdCaliper / CyPHER
Notes: Not English to bash. 28520 training pairs and 2807 test pairs of similar command lines, command against command, for training security embedding models. Listed here so we do not re-find it later. EMNLP 2024. arXiv 2411.01176. github.com/cycraft-corp/CmdCaliper

Name: CodeSift (Bash split)
Notes: This answers the question mark on the existing row. 100 unique Bash tasks with 10 generations each, so 1000 task and code pairs. IBM Research, CLOUD 2024. No public release exists, only the paper. Used as a benchmark by ScriptSmith.

Name: harpomaxx/unix-commands
Notes: Not English to bash, so do not add it as a translation set. 100 rows of 'you are a Unix terminal, produce the output', which maps a command to simulated terminal output rather than the other way round. mrheinen/linux-commands (481 rows) has the same shape.
